newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-MAS says improves aircraft usage.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-MAS says improves aircraft usage.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said on Tuesday its average daily aircraft utilisation has improved to 9.3 hours for the half-year ended September 30, 1996, from 8.4 hours during the same period a year ago.
In a statement released with its half-year results, the national carrier said its debt-to-equity ratio has further improved to 1.5 from 1.8 during the same comparative period.
MAS earlier announced its half-year net earnings were 137.11 million ringgit, down 1.7 percent from 139.48 million ringgit.
The results met analysts' expectations of flat earnings.
Turnover rose 12.8 percent during the six-month period to 3.17 billion ringgit.
Pretax profit was up 3.7 percent to 155.28 million ringgit from 149.72 million.
Analysts had expected MAS profits to be under pressure from high fuel costs. MAS said high fuel prices "will be of concern" for the rest of its financial year.
Yields will also be under continuing pressure due to prevailing excess capacity in the industry, the carrier said.
But expectations of increasing traffic demand will help the company, with the MAS board forecasting the outlook in the second half of the year to be "satisfactory".
The airline's plan to buy 25 new passenger aircraft from Boeing will enable the company to operate a young and technologically advanced fleet, it said.
"This in turn will improve yield, globalisation and customer options," MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli said in the statement.
